objective: Standard statement: on the triangular-lattice torus of side L = k m, cut every triangle of the m-torus into k^2 with shared new vertices; with copies of one knot on all triangles (S1: one placement on up triangles and one on down triangles, from the same class; 88 rules) or on up triangles (S2: 34 rules), compute for every coarse assignment the number of fine extensions (exact residues modulo four primes, floats for the support), at scale 2 on the 6- and 8-tori and at scale 3 on the 9-torus. Classify each rule as set-level exact, counted exact or neither; record solution counts on the L-torus for L = 2..12 (entropy) and whether the solution sets on the 3- to 6-tori are affine. Nearest known result: the triangular plaquette (Newman-Moore) model and the self-similarity of Pascal's triangle mod 2 under rescaling by 2; the four Baxter-Wu ground states on tori with side divisible by 3; Wannier's antiferromagnet (not-all-equal on all triangles, positive entropy); exact real-space renormalization is rare. Classification: no overlap found for the census (candidate local delta).
status: Proved by SHARED-SUBDIVISION-20261029-001A-P001 (V1, exact computation): of 122 rules (copies of one knot class on up triangles, or on all triangles with one placement per orientation), shared subdivision by 2 leaves exactly 22 exact (parity on up triangles, parity and twelve three-excluded pairs on all triangles, six twisted not-all-equal pairs) and by 3 exactly the six twisted pairs; set-level and counted exactness coincide; every exact rule has affine solution sets and at most 2^L solutions on the L-torus, every other rule a non-affine solution set; not-all-equal is never exact.
title: Which knots reproduce themselves under shared subdivision of the triangular lattice
